[[File:Figure 1- U S Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas (55336798481).jpg|thumb|alt=Aerial photo of the camp and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems outside housing units|Aerial photo of the camp and [[heating, ventilation, and air conditioning]] systems outside housing units]]
{{Immigration policy of the second Trump administration sidebar}}

'''Camp East Montana''' is the largest [[List of immigrant detention sites in the United States|immigrant detention site in the United States]],<ref name="GAO">{{cite web |title=Immigration Detention: Waste and Performance Issues at Camp East Montana Provide Valuable Lessons for Future Facilities |url=https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-26-108886 |website=[[GAO]] |language=en |date=June 9, 2026 |quote=The Army and ICE opened ICE's largest facility—Camp East Montana—quickly, which led to several issues.}}</ref> located at [[Fort Bliss]], a former [[Japanese-American internment camp]] in Texas,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Yam |first1=Kimmy |title=Japanese American groups blast use of Fort Bliss, former internment camp site, as ICE detention center |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/asian-america/fort-bliss-japanese-americans-internment-camp-immigrant-detention-rcna226044 |work=[[NBC News]] |date=August 20, 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Cuevas |first1=Eduardo |last2=Villagran |first2=Lauren |title=Army base used for WWII Japanese internment will be nation's largest ICE detention center |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2025/08/23/texas-army-base-japanese-internment-ice-detention/85767850007/ |work=[[USA TODAY]] |date=August 23, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> it opened in August 2025. The tent encampment has a planned capacity of up to 5,000 people and a contract value of around $1.2 billion.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Biesecker |first1=Michael |last2=Goodman |first2=Joshua |title=Mystery surrounds $1.2 billion Army contract to build huge detention tent camp in Texas desert |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/mystery-surrounds-1-2-billion-army-contract-to-build-huge-detention-tent-camp-in-texas-desert |work=[[pbs.org]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=August 28, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Following questions about whether Acquisition Logistics was meeting its standards, [[Amentum Services]] took over the facility on March 13, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Venegas |first=Natalie |date=2026-03-16 |title=Amentum Services named new contractor for El Paso’s Camp East Montana detention center |url=https://kfoxtv.com/news/local/amentum-services-named-new-contractor-for-el-pasos-camp-east-montana-detention-center |access-date=2026-05-25 |work=[[KFOX-TV]]}}</ref>

The camp has faced criticism over alleged human rights violations involving regular physical and sexual abuse, inedible food, malnutrition, overcrowding, medical neglect, and enforced disappearances.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Foley |first1=Ryan J. |last2=BIESECKER |first2=MICHAEL |title=ICE replaces contractor at largest detention camp after scrutiny of living conditions |url=https://apnews.com/article/ice-detention-facility-camp-east-montana-conditions-contract-c7d369ed5fcbe19d87868b9b337f5211 |work=[[AP News]] |date=March 13, 2026 |language=en |quote=The contractor switch at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas, comes as it faces scrutiny over living conditions that detainees have described as inhumane since its hasty construction and opening last year. With an average of nearly 3,000 detainees in six long tent encampments, evidence has mounted to support claims of overcrowding, medical neglect, malnutrition and emotional distress. An outbreak of measles also recently hit the camp, which several Democratic members of Congress have called for closing.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Gassama |first1=Haddy |title=Fort Bliss Passes ICE Inspection Despite Abuse and Inhumane Conditions |url=https://www.aclu.org/news/immigrants-rights/detained-immigrants-detail-physical-abuse-and-inhumane-conditions-at-largest-immigration-detention-center-in-the-u-s |work=[[American Civil Liberties Union]] |date=December 8, 2025 |language=en |quote=Interviews with 45 people at Fort Bliss report physical and sexual abuse, medical neglect, and intimidation to self-deport. The facility still passed an ICE inspection.}}</ref><ref name="Biesecker 07152026"/>

== History ==
Camp East Montana was opened on August 1, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramirez |first=Cindy |date=2025-08-18 |title=$1.2B ICE detention complex opens at Fort Bliss in East El Paso under Trump’s mass deportation strategy |url=https://elpasomatters.org/2025/08/18/ice-east-montana-detention-center-el-paso-fort-bliss-enhanced-hardened-facility/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=El Paso Matters |language=en-US}}</ref> During its first 50 days, conditions at the camp violated at least 60 federal standards, according to ICE's own detention oversight unit.<ref>{{Cite web |last=MacMillan |first=Douglas |title=60 violations in 50 days: Inside ICE’s giant tent facility at Ft. Bliss |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2025/09/16/ice-detention-center-immigration-violations/ |access-date=2025-12-13 |website=Washington Post |language=en-US}}</ref> The ACLU and other human-rights organizations called for its closure after interviewed detainees reported "physical and sexual abuse, medical neglect, and intimidation to self-deport".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detained Immigrants Detail Physical Abuse and Inhumane Conditions at Largest Immigration Detention Center in the U.S. |url=https://www.aclu.org/news/immigrants-rights/detained-immigrants-detail-physical-abuse-and-inhumane-conditions-at-largest-immigration-detention-center-in-the-u-s |access-date=2025-12-13 |website=ACLU |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Abbott |first1=Jeff |title=Exclusive: She survived ICE custody; her husband died during detention |url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/immigration/2025/12/19/immigration-news-widow-says-ice-failed-husband-in-custody/87786319007/ |access-date=28 December 2025 |work=El Paso Times |date=19 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Abbott |first1=Jeff |title=Exclusive: 911 calls from migrant detention center highlight dire conditions |url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/immigration/2025/12/20/911-calls-from-camp-east-montana-detention-center-highlight-dire-conditions/87792917007/ |access-date=28 December 2025 |work=El Paso Times |date=20 December 2025}}</ref> The contract awarded to Acquisition Logistics LLC had an estimated completion date of September 30, 2027.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2026-03-04 |title=ICE taking steps to close detention center at Fort Bliss, document shows |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/immigration/2026/03/04/trump-administration-closes-fort-bliss-detention-center/ |access-date=2026-03-05 |work=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> 

On March 3, 2026, ICE indicated that it was taking steps to close Camp East Montana after only eight months of operation.<ref name=":1" /> On March 12, 2026, the website of the [[General Services Administration]] reported that Camp East Montana would remain open, operated by [[Amentum Services, Inc.|Amentum Services Inc]]., formerly a subcontractor at the facility,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-07-25 |title=His Former Company Got Caught Employing Undocumented Workers. Now He’s Profiting Off an Immigrant Detention Camp. |url=https://www.propublica.org/article/nathan-albers-fort-bliss-immigration |access-date=2026-06-11 |work=ProPublica |language=en-US}}</ref> effective through September 30, 2026,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Foley |first=RYAN J. |date=2026-04-02 |title=Inspection finds dozens of violations of detention standards at a major immigration camp in Texas |url=https://apnews.com/article/ice-detention-facility-inspection-immigration-1f83cd2f12ba64f74fb20e46720377d7 |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> replacing Acquisition Logistics as the prime contractor providing housing, medical care, and transportation for Camp East Montana detainees.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tribune |first=Texas |date=2026-03-12 |title=Report: ICE replacing operator of El Paso’s Camp East Montana detention camp |url=https://elpasomatters.org/2026/03/12/ice-replacing-camp-east-montana-detention-center-operator-contract-washington-post/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=El Paso Matters |language=en-US}}</ref>

A [[class action]] lawsuit, ''Akari Angye et al v. ICE'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akari Angye et al v. ICE |url=https://www.aclu.org/cases/akari-angye-et-al-v-ice |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=American Civil Liberties Union |language=en-US}}</ref> was filed in May 2026 on behalf of four detainees, for inhumane conditions at the facility. A June 2026 [[United States Government Accountability Office|Government Accountability Office]] (GAO) [[Watchdog#Public oversight|watchdog]] report also outlined "significant, pervasive" federal standards violations persisting under operator Amentum Services, after replacing Acquisition Logistics, including use of violent force and severe medical neglect.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=MacMillan |first=Douglas |date=2026-06-09 |title=ICE detention camp endangered migrants and wasted millions, watchdog finds |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/06/09/ice-detention-camp-wasted-millions-endangered-migrants-gao-finds/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |work=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

=== Deaths and human rights violations ===
By December 2025, more than 45 detainees had reported abuse and injuries to their attorneys.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeGuzman |first=Lomi Kriel, Colleen |date=2026-02-26 |title=Escobar leads Dems' call for ICE to close El Paso camp |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/02/26/democrats-veronica-escobar-detention-deaths-texas-east-montana-campos/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> Two inmates reported having their testicles crushed by guards as a form of punishment.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Figueroa |first=Lorena |date=2025-12-09 |title=Officers at Texas immigration detention facility accused of beatings and sexual abuse |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/dec/09/texas-ice-camp-abuse-immigration |access-date=2026-01-23 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

{{As of|2026|01}}, three detainee deaths were reported within a 44 days.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-19 |title=Third immigrant detainee at facility in El Paso has died, ICE says |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/third-immigrant-detainee-facility-el-paso-died-ice-says-rcna254783 |access-date=2026-01-20 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref> An autopsy ruled the death of 55-year old Cuban immigrant [[Killing of Geraldo Lunas Campos|Geraldo Lunas Campos]] as a homicide caused by [[asphyxia]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Bedoya |first=Aaron A. |title=Homicide at ICE facility sparks El Paso mayor’s call for investigation |url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/news/immigration/2026/01/22/el-paso-mayor-renard-johnson-calls-investigation-immigrant-homicide-at-ice-camp-east-montana/88309005007/ |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=El Paso Times |language=en-US}}</ref> ICE officials stated that his death was a suicide while in [[solitary confinement]], but witnesses told press that he had been handcuffed and choked by guards before his death.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Biesecker |first=Michael |last2=Foley |first2=Ryan |date=2026-01-22 |title=Autopsy finds Cuban immigrant in ICE custody died of homicide due to asphyxia |url=https://apnews.com/article/ice-immigration-detention-death-texas-f04b5cb76f175255e58b947f0e14bc12 |access-date=2026-01-22 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Canon |first=Gabrielle |date=2026-01-16 |title=Death of man at ICE camp could be investigated as homicide after examiner’s report |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jan/15/ice-detention-camp-texas-death |access-date=2026-01-21 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>After the El Paso medical examiner ruled Campos' death a homicide, El Paso mayor [[Renard Johnson]] called for an independent investigation.<ref name=":0" /> The June 2026 GAO report included its investigation into Campos’ death, states that Acquisition Logistics failed to document the incident in its reports to ICE, and that related documentary evidence “was missing or destroyed”.<ref name=":2" /> Individuals attempting to visit detainees from [[Operation Metro Surge|Minneapolis]], where Lunas Campos had been detained, were told those inmates were no longer allowed to have visitors.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Moore |first1=Robert |last2=Ramirez |first2=Cindy |title=Minnesota detainees denied visitors at Fort Bliss following 3rd death at ICE facility |url=https://elpasomatters.org/2026/01/18/third-death-suicide-ice-custody-camp-east-montana-el-paso-texas-fort-bliss/ |access-date=21 January 2026 |work=El Paso Matters |date=18 January 2026}}</ref>

On January 14, Victor Manuel Diaz died while detained at Camp East Montana, said by ICE to be due to "presumed suicide".<ref name="Foley">{{cite web |last1=Foley |first1=Ryan J. |title=Cuban immigrant in ICE custody died of homicide due to asphyxia, autopsy finds |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/cuban-immigrant-in-ice-custody-died-of-homicide-due-to-asphyxia-autopsy-finds |website=PBS News |language=en-us |date=22 January 2026}}</ref> Unlike the previous two detainees who had autopsies performed by the local county medical examiner, Diaz's body was transferred to the [[William Beaumont Army Medical Center]] under the jurisdiction of the federal government.<ref name="Foley"/><ref name="Venegas">{{cite web |last1=Venegas |first1=Natalie |title=Migrant death at Camp East Montana raises concerns over body transfer to military hospital |url=https://cbs4local.com/newsletter-daily/migrant-death-at-camp-east-montana-raises-concerns-over-body-transfer-to-military-hospital |website=KDBC |language=en |date=24 January 2026}}</ref>

At the end of January 2026, Victor Manuel Diaz's family questioned the information provided by ICE, pointing out that the agency had not sent them detailed information about Victor's death and describing the procedures as "suspicious" and irregular, leading them to launch an independent investigation to clarify the case.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title='I don't believe he took his life': Family of Nicaraguan man seeks answers after his death in ICE detention facility |url=https://abcnews.com/US/dont-life-family-nicaraguan-man-seeks-answers-after/story?id=129497484 |access-date=2026-02-12 |website=ABC News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Family questions federal investigation of Nicaraguan migrant’s death at Camp East Montana |url=https://www.borderreport.com/news/family-questions-federal-investigation-of-nicaraguan-migrants-death-at-camp-east-montana/ |website=BorderReport}}</ref>

A 2026 report by [[Human Rights Watch]] and the [[American Civil Liberties Union]] described alleged human rights abuses at the camp including frequent beatings and their use for collective punishment, filthy conditions, inedible food, and denied medical care and legal representation. It wrote that in some cases, inmates were threatened with violence, criminal prosecution, and indefinite detention if they did not give up their immigration claims which would "potentially qualify" as enforced disappearances and a violation of international human rights law. In a statement, the Department of Homeland Security called the allegations "categorically false".<ref name="Biesecker 07152026">{{Cite news|last=Biesecker|first=Michael|date=July 15, 2026|title=Report: Detainees at ICE facility in Texas report frequent beatings and other human rights abuses|work=AP News|url=https://apnews.com/article/ice-camp-detention-trump-homeland-security-dhs-immigration-deaths-abuse-30ec92636a5601b0071895efa871b990|access-date=July 16, 2026}}</ref>

=== Health conditions ===
On February 10, 2026, ''[[The Irish Times]]'' published an article based on an interview with Seamus Culleton, one of the people detained by ICE in Boston, about the conditions at Camp East Montana, where he mentioned that food was quite scarce and that there were frequent fights among detainees to obtain food. He also mentioned that the camp did not have adequate laundry facilities and that many of the women were forced to wear dirty clothes for several weeks. Culleton described the facility as a concentration camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Connell |first=Cian |title=Ice detention camp, where Irishman is held, under scrutiny for unexplained deaths |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/world/us/2026/02/10/ice-detention-camp-where-irishman-is-held-under-scrutiny-for-unexplained-deaths/ |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=The Irish Times |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Reporter |first=Elyse WanshelSenior |last2=HuffPost |date=2026-02-10 |title=It’s A 'Modern-Day Concentration Camp': Irish Man Held By ICE Details 'Nightmare' Facility |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/modern-day-concentration-camp-irish-man-held-by-ice_n_698b4342e4b0073b47aaf185 |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=HuffPost |language=en}}</ref> Culleton had previously been detained by ICE following reports of drug possession charges in Ireland that date back to 2009.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Carroll |first=Rory |last2= |first2= |date=2026-02-12 |title=Irishman held by ICE was issued warrant over 2009 drug offense in Ireland |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/feb/12/seamus-culleton-ice-detention-ireland-drug-charges |access-date=2026-02-14 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Keena |first=Colm |title=Seamus Culleton was facing drug charges at the time he moved to United States |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/ireland/2026/02/12/seamus-culleton-was-facing-drugs-charges-at-the-time-he-moved-to-united-states/ |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=The Irish Times |language=en}}</ref>

On February 7, 2026, it was discovered that poor sanitation at Camp East Montana had helped spread disease within the facilities, including two cases of [[tuberculosis]] and 18 cases of [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-02-07 |title=Two tuberculosis cases detected at Camp East Montana ICE facility |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/02/07/ice-facility-el-paso-tuberculosis/ |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> Alarms about poor healthcare for immigrants were raised by Democrat [[Veronica Escobar]], who reported that one-third of detainees have a chronic illness and around 200 to 300 need daily [[insulin]], stating that conditions at Camp East Montana are deteriorating to the point of violating basic human rights.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeGuzman |first=Colleen |date=2026-02-09 |title=Tuberculosis and COVID-19 Detected at Camp East Montana ICE Jail in El Paso |url=https://truthout.org/articles/tuberculosis-and-covid-19-detected-at-camp-east-montana-ice-jail-in-el-paso/ |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=Truthout |language=en-US}}</ref> One woman detained at the camp had been due for surgery to remove an [[ovarian cyst]] when ICE arrested her in Minneapolis without a warrant; she was not receiving medications while in detention.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nesterak |first1=Max |title=‘I feel desperate’: Minnesota woman suffering medical emergency stuck in Texas detention |url=https://minnesotareformer.com/2026/03/16/i-feel-desperate-minnesota-woman-suffering-medical-emergency-stuck-in-texas-detention/ |access-date=16 March 2026 |work=Minnesota Reformer |date=16 March 2026}}</ref>

Escobar pointed out that Camp East Montana had many immigrants in poor health, citing cases of pregnant women who had lost a lot of weight due to malnutrition while in ICE custody. She also noted that some immigrants had collapsed during her visit on January 29.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Salhotra |first=Pooja |last2=Ulloa |first2=Jazmine |date=2026-02-05 |title=Trump’s Migrant Detention Pipeline Extends From Minnesota to El Paso |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/05/us/minnesota-el-paso-ice-immigration.html |access-date=2026-02-12 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> On March 3, 2026, Camp East Montana was closed to visitors due to a [[measles]] outbreak, with the center reporting 14 active measles cases.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nguyen |first=Lomi Kriel, Alex |date=2026-03-04 |title=14 measles cases reported at El Paso ICE tent camp |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/03/03/texas-ice-detention-measles-east-montana-dilley-el-paso/ |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

On March 30, ''[[NPR]]'' reported that about 50 calls to emergency services were made from the camp during January and February 2026. A woman who was formerly held at the site and developed a fever while there said that there was a wait list for detainees to access the onsite clinic, and that the clinic staff often prescribed water for a wide range of conditions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kocherga |first=Angela |date=2026-03-30 |title=Emergency calls reveal conditions at the nation's largest immigration detention camp |url=https://www.npr.org/2026/03/30/nx-s1-5755003/emergency-calls-reveal-conditions-at-the-nations-largest-immigration-detention-camp |access-date=2026-04-01 |work=NPR |language=en}}</ref>

The June 2026 [[United States Government Accountability Office|Government Accountability Office]] report detailed extreme medical neglect, including failure to treat detainees with HIV and diabetes and to prevent a measles outbreak over several months, with at least 14 individuals infected.<ref name=":2" />

In October 2026, several attorneys and experts raised concerns about Camp East Montana, citing inhumane conditions reported by former detainees; explaining that ICE has mistreated immigrants within the facilities, where it is alleged that some guards have verbally abused detainees and basic hygiene services have been cut back, resulting in poor sanitary conditions throughout much of the facility, where detainees are forced to live in an environment contaminated with feces and urine, and access to soap and toilets is severely limited. Court filings also clarified that, due to the poor sanitary conditions at the facility, mice and insects have begun to infiltrate the camp, worsening the detainees’ medical condition.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Villarreal |first=Alexandra |date=2026-10-16 |title=‘Unsafe’ conditions at Texas ICE facility put immigrants at risk of injury or death, lawsuit says |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/16/texas-ice-facility-immigrants-risks-lawsuit |access-date=2026-10-17 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

In addition, testimonies from former detainees also describe problems with food distribution within the camp, where some witnesses state that they were forced to eat cookies, candy, and potato chips instead of proper meals; which caused them to lose a lot of weight and led to a deterioration in their health.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aghomo |first=Meredith McKelvey, Max Mazoch, Oisakhose |date=2026-09-02 |title=ICE Contractor for Controversial Camp East Montana Is Trailed by Fraud Allegations |url=https://www.texasobserver.org/ice-contractor-camp-east-montana-el-paso/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=The Texas Observer |language=en-US}}</ref> Some former detainees told The Guardian that sometimes the food distributed by DHS agents was rotten, and that on certain occasions, food rations were so limited that people were forced to starve.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Villarreal |first=Alexandra |date=2026-04-15 |title=‘Psychological torture’: outcry over conditions at ICE desert detention camp |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/15/ice-desert-detention-camp-east-montana |access-date=2026-10-18 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Witnesses interviewed by Human Rights Watch noted that their health had significantly deteriorated during their stay at Camp East Montana. An Ecuadorian immigrant stated that she was at risk of permanently losing her vision because DHS agents failed to provide her with medical care for her contact lenses, while a Cuban immigrant explained that he had developed ulcers during his stay and that agents had refused to treat him after multiple requests. <ref>{{Cite journal |last=César |first=Angélica |date=2026-07-15 |title=“You’re Only Getting Out Deported or Dead” |url=https://www.hrw.org/report/2026/07/15/youre-only-getting-out-deported-or-dead/abusive-us-immigration-detention-at-ft |journal=Human Rights Watch |language=en}}</ref>

== Public reactions ==
Spanish-language outlets, such as ''[[La Nación]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-20 |title=Así es el “Alligator Alcatraz” de Texas: Camp East Montana, el centro del ICE donde murieron tres migrantes bajo custodia |url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/estados-unidos/texas/asi-es-el-alligator-alcatraz-de-texas-camp-east-montana-el-centro-del-ice-donde-murieron-tres-nid20012026/ |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=LA NACION |language=es}}</ref> ''[[Univision]],''<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-19 |title=Así es el Camp East Montana, en Fort Bliss, donde han muerto 3 inmigrantes y organizaciones exigen su cierre {{!}} N+ Univision Mundo {{!}} Univision |url=https://www.univision.com/noticias/mundo/asi-es-el-camp-east-montana-en-fort-bliss-donde-han-muerto-3-inmigrantes-y-organizaciones-exigen-su-cierre |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=www.univision.com |language=es |quote=El Camp East Montana ha sido comparado con 'Alligator Alcatraz'}}</ref> and ''[[El Tiempo (Colombia)|El Tiempo]],''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guevara |first=Laura Juliana Castellanos |date=2025-08-21 |title=Así es Camp East Montana, el nuevo centro de detención de migrantes más grande de EE. UU.: carpas sin aislamiento térmico en temperaturas de 40 grados |url=https://www.eltiempo.com/mundo/eeuu-y-canada/asi-es-camp-east-montana-el-nuevo-centro-de-detencion-de-migrantes-mas-grande-de-estados-unidos-carpas-sin-aislamiento-termico-bajo-temperaturas-de-40-grados-3483067 |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=El Tiempo |language=spanish}}</ref> dubbed Camp East Montana the "[[Alligator Alcatraz]] of Texas", referring to the facility in [[Florida]], after comparisons were made to how poorly the facility was designed, reporting that the facility had broken bathrooms as well as poor food and medicine supply systems, in addition to the fact that it had been put into operation while it was still under construction. According to [[Andrea Pitzer]], author of ''One Long Night, a history of concentration camps'', conditions at the [[Everglades]] camp<ref>{{Cite magazine |title=The Grand Opening of an American Concentration Camp |first=Melissa Gira|last=Grant|url=https://newrepublic.com/article/197508/alligator-alcatraz-trump-concentration-camp |date=2025-07-02 |magazine=The New Republic |issn=0028-6583}}</ref> and at Camp East Montana are integral to an increase in domestic and international concentration camps.<ref>Pitzer, Andrea (April 7, 2026) [https://degenerateart.beehiiv.com/p/planet-of-the-camps Planet of the campsThe U.S. is imposing an international network of concentration camps on the world].</ref>

In January 2026, a coalition of immigrant rights organizations in New Mexico and Texas, including Las Americas Immigrant Advocacy Center, Contigo Immigrant Justice, Estrella del Paso, and the [[Border Network for Human Rights]] (BNHR), issued a statement calling for the closure of the facilities after multiple incidents involving the deaths of Latinos in the camp and DHS violations of basic procedures for treating people.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-20 |title=Groups demand immediate closure of Camp East Montana following 3rd in-custody death |url=https://www.borderreport.com/news/groups-demand-immediate-closure-of-camp-east-montana-following-3rd-in-custody-death/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260120165956/https://www.borderreport.com/news/groups-demand-immediate-closure-of-camp-east-montana-following-3rd-in-custody-death/ |archive-date=2026-01-20 |access-date=2026-01-25 |work=BorderReport |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Human Rights Groups Urge ICE to End Immigration Detention at Fort Bliss Military Base, Halt Abusive Third-Country Deportations |url=https://www.nmilc.org/our-blog/campeastmontanaletter |access-date=2026-01-25 |website=NMILC |language=en-US}}</ref>

On February 11, 2026, several Texas lawmakers called attention to how Camp East Montana was being operated, implying that the facilities were torturing immigrants and violating basic protocols for the treatment of people. They also compared the treatment of Latinos to the [[Internment of Japanese Americans]] at Fort Bliss. Thirty-six Democrats in the Texas State House, including [[Ana-Maria Ramos]], had called for investigations into Camp East Montana to prevent the death of people in the facilities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Texas Lawmakers Sound Alarm on 'Torture, Killing, and Inhumane Treatment' of Detainees in Fort Bliss ICE Facility {{!}} Common Dreams |url=https://www.commondreams.org/news/fort-bliss-inhumane-ice-conditions |access-date=2026-02-12 |website=www.commondreams.org |language=en}}</ref>

On February 26, 2026, more than two dozen Democrats in the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]], led by Congresswoman Escobar, sent a letter to the Department of Homeland Security, calling on the Trump administration to close Camp East Montana, due to safety and health problems at the facility.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeGuzman |first=Lomi Kriel, Colleen |date=2026-02-26 |title=Escobar leads Dems' call for ICE to close El Paso camp |url=https://www.texastribune.org/2026/02/26/democrats-veronica-escobar-detention-deaths-texas-east-montana-campos/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=The Texas Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> In late March, US representative [[Kelly Morrison]] paid an unannounced oversight visit to the facility. She described "unbelievably inhumane" conditions there, though she was not permitted to speak to or leave a note for the detainees.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nesterak |first1=Max |title=‘Unbelievably inhumane’: U.S. Rep. Kelly Morrison visits troubled Texas detention center |url=https://minnesotareformer.com/2026/03/25/unbelievably-inhumane-u-s-rep-kelly-morrison-visits-troubled-texas-detention-center/ |access-date=27 March 2026 |work=Minnesota Reformer |date=25 March 2026}}</ref>

The June 2026 [[GAO]] report detailed extreme medical neglect, including failure to treat detainees with HIV and diabetes, or to prevent a measles outbreak over several months, with at least 14 individuals infected.<ref>{{Cite news |last=MacMillan|first=Douglas|date=2026-06-09|title=ICE detention camp endangered migrants and wasted millions, watchdog finds|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/06/09/ice-detention-camp-wasted-millions-endangered-migrants-gao-finds/|access-date=2026-06-11|work=The Washington Post|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

In October 2026, [[Rochelle Mercedes Garza]], president of the Texas Civil Rights Project, issued a statement regarding Camp East Montana, in which she clarified that "State-sanctioned violence is occurring in and outside of facilities like Camp East Montana, and the blatant disregard for human life and access to basic health care should shock the conscience of every American".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Legal Organizations Urge Federal Court to End Abuse and Deadly Conditions and Protect People Detained at Camp East Montana |url=https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/legal-organizations-urge-federal-court-to-end-abuse-and-deadly-conditions-and-protect-people-detained-at-camp-east-montana |access-date=2026-10-17 |website=American Civil Liberties Union |language=en-US}}</ref>
